solution: Let slopes be \(m\) and \(m^2\). For \(ax^2+2hxy+by^2=0\): \(m+m^2=-\dfrac{2h}{b}\) and \(m\cdot m^2=m^3=\dfrac{a}{b}\). Then \((m+m^2)^3=m^3+m^6+3m\cdot m^2(m+m^2)=m^3+(m^3)^2+3m^3(m+m^2)\). So \(\left(-\dfrac{2h}{b}\right)^3=\dfrac{a}{b}+\dfrac{a^2}{b^2}+3\dfrac{a}{b}\left(-\dfrac{2h}{b}\right)\). Multiply by \(b^3\): \(-8h^3=ab^2+a^2b-6abh\), i.e. \(a^2b+ab^2+8h^3=6abh\). Hence proved.
note: removed four sentences of scratch work ('is messy; instead use m^3 + m^6?', '(m^2)^{3/2}...') between the slope relations and the cube identity; the proof itself was complete and right.
